features.name: Toxic Tradecraft
features.entriesHtml:
You gain a Poisoner's Kit, and you have proficiency with it. In addition, your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus is doubled for ability checks with a Poisoner's Kit. If you lose the kit, you can harvest toxic flora and venomous fauna for 1 hour to magically create a replacement. This harvest can be performed during a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB, and it destroys the previous Poisoner's Kit.

Once per turn when you deal Poison damage to a creature with a weapon attack, you can expend a spell slot (no action required). The attack deals an extra 1d6 Poison damage and the target gains the Poisoned condition until the end of your next turn. You may also add a Toxin Effect, chosen from the appropriate list below. All Toxin Effects last until the end of your next turn, unless its description states otherwise.

Level 1 Spell Slot Effects.

When you expend a level 1+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

Attenuate.

While a creature has the Poisoned condition from this toxin, it has Disadvantage|XPHB on Strength and Dexterity saving throws.

Befuddled.

While a creature has the Poisoned condition from this toxin, it can't speak, read, or write and it has Disadvantage|XPHB on saving throws made to maintain Concentration|XPHB on spells.

Uncoordinated.

While a creature has the Poisoned condition from this toxin, it can't take Reaction|XPHB|Reactions or the Disengage or Dodge action.

Level 2 Spell Slot Effects.

When you expend a level 2+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

Debilitate.

For 1 minute, the creature can't regain Hit Points|XPHB.

Potent.

For 1 minute, the creature loses Resistance|XPHB to Poison damage.

Suffer.

For 1 minute, the first time on each turn the creature takes Poison damage, it takes an extra 1d6 Poison damage.

Level 3 Spell Slot Effects.

When you expend a level 3+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

Lingering.

Instead of ending at the end of your next turn, the creature has the Poisoned condition for 10 minutes. During this time it has Disadvantage|XPHB on saving throws to end the Poisoned condition on itself. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw to end the Poisoned condition.

Supernatural.

When you deal damage to a creature with a poisoned item, the creature loses Immunity|XPHB to the Poisoned condition and then has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw to end the Poisoned condition and regain its Immunity|XPHB to the Poisoned condition.

Level 4 Spell Slot Effects.

When you expend a level 4+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

Flesh Eating.

For 1 minute, the creature has the Poisoned condition. While a creature has the Posioned condition from this toxin, it takes 2d6 Acid damage at the start of each of its turns.

Insensate.

While a creature has the Poisoned condition from this toxin, it also has the Blinded and Deafened conditions.

Paraplegia.

While a creature has the Poisoned condition from this toxin, its Speed|XPHB is reduced to 0 and it has Disadvantage|XPHB on Dexterity saving throws.

Level 5 Spell Slot Effects.

When you expend a level 5 spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

Enhanced.

Apply one option from the Level 4 Spell Slot Effects list, and an additional option from either the Level 1 or Level 2 Spell Slot Effects list.

Stinging Application.

For 1 minute, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a poisoned item, the attack deals an extra 5d6 damage. The damage type is your choice of Acid, Necrotic, or Poison.

At the end of each of the creature's turns, it can make a Constitution saving throw to end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition and regain its {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

rawEntries.name: Level 4 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 4+ spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Flesh Eating
entries: For 1 minute, the creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. While a creature has the Posioned condition from this toxin, it takes {@damage 2d6} Acid damage at the start of each of its turns.

entries.name: Insensate
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, it also has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} and {@condition Deafened|XPHB} conditions.

entries.name: Paraplegia
entries: While a creature has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition from this toxin, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 and it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws.

rawEntries.name: Level 5 Spell Slot Effects
entries: When you expend a level 5 spell slot, choose one of the following effects to add to the toxin.

entries.name: Enhanced
entries: Apply one option from the Level 4 Spell Slot Effects list, and an additional option from either the Level 1 or Level 2 Spell Slot Effects list.

entries.name: Stinging Application
entries: For 1 minute, once per turn, when you hit a creature with a {@condition poisoned} item, the attack deals an extra {@damage 5d6} damage. The damage type is your choice of Acid, Necrotic, or Poison.

features.name: Poison Control
features.entriesHtml:
You gain Resistance|XPHB to Poison damage and have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.

In addition, you can cast the Protection from Poison spell without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

In addition, you can cast the {@spell Protection from Poison|XPHB} spell without expending a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

features.name: Variegated Vexations
features.entriesHtml: Whenever you would deal Poison damage with a weapon attack, you can change that damage to be either Acid or Necrotic instead.
rawEntries: Whenever you would deal Poison damage with a weapon attack, you can change that damage to be either Acid or Necrotic instead.

features.name: Pain Tolerance
features.entriesHtml: You have learned to quickly inure yourself against harm. Immediately before you take damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to gain Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to the damage you take. If any of these Temporary Hit Points|XPHB remain at the end of your next turn, they vanish.

Immediately before you take damage from a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage you take. If any of these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} remain at the end of your next turn, they vanish.

features.name: Grim Harbinger
features.entriesHtml:
Seal Fate as an Omen of Doom

Grim harbingers wander places touched by death, serving as both a watcher of the dead and the herald of doom for those whose lives are running out. At their side is a guardian spirit and omen of death known as a grim, a constant companion that aids in performing their shared, grave duty.

features.name: Omen of Doom
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you target a creature you can see within 90 feet of you and magically seal its doom for 1 hour. Once per turn when you hit the doomed target with an attack, it takes an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage.

In addition, a ghostly creature called the Grim appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the target. Grims most often appear as black, spectral hounds, but you can choose an appearance appropriate to its stat block.

The grim is Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly to you and your allies, and it obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die, when the doomed creature dies, when it is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, or when you use this feature again.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB. You can also expend a spell slot to restore an expended use (no action required).

The Grim in Combat.

In combat, the grim acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction|XPHB on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also command it as part of the Bonus Action|XPHB you take to use Omen of Doom, or you can sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the grim to take the Ominous Rend action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the grim acts on its own and is not limited to the Dodge action.

In addition, a ghostly creature called the {@creature Grim|CrookedMoon24} appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the target. Grims most often appear as black, spectral hounds, but you can choose an appearance appropriate to its stat block.

The grim is {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} to you and your allies, and it obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die, when the doomed creature dies, when it is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, or when you use this feature again.

features.name: Harbinger of Doom
features.entriesHtml:
Your control over doom grows stronger, granting the following benefits.

Graveyard Hunter.

The Grim Ominous Rend action deals an extra 1d6 Necrotic damage on a hit.

Mortal Reminder.

When you deal damage to a creature doomed by your Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24, you can change the damage type to Necrotic.

Mounting Dread.

Necrotic damage dealt by you or the grim ignores Resistance|XPHB.

features.name: Grave Bond
features.entriesHtml:
You draw deeper strength from the grave. You gain the following benefits.

Ghastly Hound.

The grim gains Resistance|XPHB to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Grave Fortitude.

You gain Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage.

Inescapable Fate.

When the target of your Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 succeeds on a saving throw, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force it to reroll the save with Disadvantage|XPHB and use the new roll. Once you cause a save to fail with this benefit, you can't use it again until the current Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 ends.

Jaws of Doom.

On a failed save, until the current Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 ends, the target has Vulnerability|XPHB to damage dealt by the grim and to the extra damage you deal with Omen of Doom|Ranger|XPHB|Grim Harbinger|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 4+ spell slot (no action required).

features.name: Hollow Warden
features.entriesHtml:
Draw on the Might of Ancient Wild Terrors

Legends tell that the most ancient and bloodthirsty terrors lurk deep within the old places of the earth. Hollow Wardens venerate and draw power from such beings, transforming themselves into merciless and monstrous guardians that stalk jagged coastlines, steep mountain crags, and other dark and wild places.

features.name: Wrath of the Wild
features.entriesHtml:
You draw power from the strange and ancient horrors of the land, causing you to sprout unnatural growths, such as bloody antlers or putrid fangs, or causing your shadow to lengthen or twist around you. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can expend a use of Favored Enemy|Ranger|XPHB|1 to transform into a ghastly form, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute or until you have the Incapacitated condition, die, or end the transformation (no action required).

Ancient Armor.

You gain a +1 bonus to AC, as your body is wreathed in rotten bark and beastly bristles. This bonus increases to +2 when you reach Ranger level 11.

Prowling Retribution.

Immediately after a creature you can see within 5 feet of yourself deals damage to you or one of your allies, you can make an Opportunity Attack against that creature.

Unnerving Aura.

When you transform and at the start of each of your subsequent turns, each creature of your choice in a 10-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation originating from you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature has the Frightened condition until the start of your next turn.

On a failed save, a creature has the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Hungering Might
features.entriesHtml:
You gain a bonus to Constitution saving throws equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

In addition, once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll while you are transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to 1d10 plus your Wisdom modifier, provided you are Bloodied|XPHB when you hit.

In addition, once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll while you are transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to {@dice 1d10} plus your Wisdom modifier, provided you are {@status Bloodied|XPHB} when you hit.

features.name: Rot and Violence
features.entriesHtml:
Your dedication to wild eldritch beings alters you further. When transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you gain the following additional benefits.

Menacing Aura.

When a creature fails its saving throw against your Unnerving Aura, it also can't regain Hit Points|XPHB or take Reaction|XPHB|Reactions until the start of your next turn.

Strangling Roots.

When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can activate the Sap or Slow mastery property in addition to a different mastery property you're using with that weapon.

features.name: Ancient Might
features.entriesHtml:
You become wholly suffused with the wild's ancient and terrible power, granting you the following benefits.

Ominous Strikes.

When you hit a creature that has the Frightened condition with an attack roll, that attack deals extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

Persistent Wrath.

If you're reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB but not killed outright while transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you can surge with wild power. Your Hit Points|XPHB instead change to a number equal to twice your Ranger level. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also expend a level 4+ spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of this feature.

Timeless.

You have Immunity|XPHB to the Exhaustion condition.

features.name: Detect Portal
features.entriesHtml:
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to magically sense the presence of a planar portal. As an action, you detect the distance and direction to the closest planar portal within 1 mile of you.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

See the "Planar Travel" section in chapter 2 of the Dungeon Master's Guide for examples of planar portals.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
See the "Planar Travel" section in chapter 2 of the Dungeon Master's Guide for examples of planar portals.

features.name: Horizon Walker
features.entriesHtml: Horizon Walkers guard the world against threats that originate from other planes or that seek to ravage the mortal realm with otherworldly magic. They seek out planar portals and keep watch over them, venturing to the Inner Planes and the Outer Planes as needed to pursue their foes. These rangers are also friends to any forces in the multiverse—especially benevolent dragons, fey, and elementals—that work to preserve life and the order of the planes.

They seek out planar portals and keep watch over them, venturing to the Inner Planes and the Outer Planes as needed to pursue their foes. These rangers are also friends to any forces in the multiverse—especially benevolent dragons, fey, and elementals—that work to preserve life and the order of the planes.

9thhaste

features.name: Planar Warrior
features.entriesHtml:
At 3rd level, you learn to draw on the energy of the multiverse to augment your attacks.

As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The next time you hit that creature on this turn with a weapon attack, all damage dealt by the attack becomes force damage, and the creature takes an extra 1d8 force damage from the attack. When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d8}.

features.name: Ethereal Step
features.entriesHtml:
At 7th level, you learn to step through the Ethereal Plane. As a bonus action, you can cast the etherealness spell with this feature, without expending a spell slot, but the spell ends at the end of the current turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Distant Strike
features.entriesHtml:
At 11th level, you gain the ability to pass between the planes in the blink of an eye. When you take the Attack action, you can teleport up to 10 feet before each attack to an unoccupied space you can see.

If you attack at least two different creatures with the action, you can make one additional attack with it against a third creature.

features.name: Spectral Defense
features.entriesHtml: At 15th level, your ability to move between planes enables you to slip through the planar boundaries to lessen the harm done to you during battle. When you take damage from an attack, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to all of that attack's damage on this turn.

features.name: Hunter
features.entriesHtml:
Protect Nature and People from Destruction

You stalk prey in the wilds and elsewhere, using your abilities as a Hunter to protect nature and people everywhere from forces that would destroy them.
rawEntries: {@i Protect Nature and People from Destruction}
You stalk prey in the wilds and elsewhere, using your abilities as a Hunter to protect nature and people everywhere from forces that would destroy them.

features.name: Hunter's Lore
features.entriesHtml: You can call on the forces of nature to reveal certain strengths and weaknesses of your prey. While a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, you know whether that creature has any Immunities, Resistances, or Vulnerabilities, and if the creature has any, you know what they are.

features.name: Hunter's Prey
features.entriesHtml:
You gain one of the following feature options of your choice. Whenever you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB, you can replace the chosen option with the other one.

Colossus Slayer.

Your tenacity can wear down even the most resilient foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon, the weapon deals an extra 1d8 damage to the target if it's missing any of its Hit Points|XPHB. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.

Horde Breaker.

Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target, that is within the weapon's range, and that you haven't attacked this turn.

Multiattack Defense.

When a creature hits you with an attack roll, that creature has Disadvantage|XPHB on all other attack rolls against you this turn.

features.name: Hunter's Sense
features.entriesHtml:
At 3rd level, you gain the ability to peer at a creature and magically discern how best to hurt it. As an action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you. You immediately learn whether the creature has any damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities and what they are. If the creature is hidden from divination magic, you sense that it has no damage immunities, resistances, or vulnerabilities.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Monster Slayer
features.entriesHtml: You have dedicated yourself to hunting down creatures of the night and wielders of grim magic. A Monster Slayer seeks out vampires, dragons, evil fey, fiends, and other magical threats. Trained in supernatural techniques to overcome such monsters, slayers are experts at unearthing and defeating mighty, mystical foes.

features.name: Slayer's Prey
features.entriesHtml:
Starting at 3rd level, you can focus your ire on one foe, increasing the harm you inflict on it. As a bonus action, you designate one creature you can see within 60 feet of you as the target of this feature. The first time each turn that you hit that target with a weapon attack, it takes an extra 1d6 damage from the weapon.

This benefit lasts until you finish a short or long rest. It ends early if you designate a different creature.

features.name: Supernatural Defense
features.entriesHtml: At 7th level, you gain extra resilience against your prey's assaults on your mind and body. Whenever the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw and whenever you make an ability check to escape that target's grapple, add 1d6 to your roll.

features.name: Magic-User's Nemesis
features.entriesHtml:
At 11th level, you gain the ability to thwart someone else's magic. When you see a creature casting a spell or teleporting within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction to try to magically foil it. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or its spell or teleport fails and is wasted.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

features.name: Slayer's Counter
features.entriesHtml: At 15th level, you gain the ability to counterattack when your prey tries to sabotage you. If the target of your Slayer's Prey forces you to make a saving throw, you can use your reaction to make one weapon attack against the quarry. You make this attack immediately before making the saving throw. If your attack hits, your save automatically succeeds, in addition to the attack's normal effects.

features.name: Elemental Arrows
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can imbue a Longbow or Shortbow with elemental energy for 1 minute. Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. For the duration, the imbued weapon deals damage of the selected type instead of its normal type and deals an extra 1d6 damage of the chosen type when it hits. At the start of each of your turns, you can change this choice.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Herbal Lore
features.entriesHtml:
You gain an Herbalism Kit and are proficient with it. You can use the Herbalism Kit as a Bonus Action|XPHB to stabilize an Unconscious creature within 5 feet of you that has 0 Hit Points|XPHB as if using a Healer's Kit without needing to make a Wisdom (Medicine) check. If you take a Utilize action, an Unconscious creature within 5 feet of you that has 0 Hit Points|XPHB gains 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point instead.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Primordial Archer
features.entriesHtml:
Channel the Wrath of the Wilds

In the areas of Etharis where nature still holds sway, many cling to the ancient customs of woodland hunters and witches. Marking themselves with wild plants and bone needles, theirs is a tradition of cunning, cruelty, and reprisal against all trespassers. Unlike the Druids, these wood witches twist natural magic into hexes, imbuing their weapons with nature's fury.

features.entriesHtml: With 1 hour of work or when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can use an Herbalism Kit to mark yourself with elemental patterns. You gain Resistance|XPHB to one of the following damage types of your choice until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

features.name: Witching Arrows
features.entriesHtml:
You gain the ability to imbue curses into your arrows. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a ranged attack using a Longbow or Shortbow, you can expend a level 1+ spell slot to choose one of the following effects (no action required). The listed damage increases by 2d6 for each spell slot above 1.

Arcing Shot.

Electricity crackles around the arrow. Make a ranged attack roll with the same weapon against a second creature within 30 feet of the first that is also within your range. Each creature hit takes 2d6 Lightning damage.

Entangling Shot.

The wooden shaft of the arrow sprouts tiny green leaves. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 Piercing damage and has the Restrained condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes the damage only. A Restrained creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Hexing Shot.

The magic surrounding your arrow clouds the mind of your target. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 Psychic damage and gains the Charmed or Frightened condition for 1 minute (your choice). The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

Viper Shot.

The arrow transforms into a hissing serpent. The target must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target takes 2d6 Poison damage and has the Poisoned condition for 1 minute. The creature can repeat the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only.

features.entriesHtml:
Taking damage can't break your Concentration|XPHB on any Ranger spells you cast.

In addition, you can take a Bonus Action|XPHB to change the damage type you chose for the Weave the Elements feature to a different damage type in the list. When you do, you can choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. That creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 6d6 damage of the either damage type (your choice).

features.name: Gathered Swarm
features.entriesHtml:
3rd-level Swarmkeeper feature

A swarm of intangible nature spirits has bonded itself to you and can assist you in battle. While you're alive, the swarm remains in your space, crawling on you or flying and skittering around you within your space. You determine its appearance, or you generate its appearance by rolling on the Swarm Appearance table.

d4Appearance
1Swarming insects
2Miniature twig blights
3Fluttering birds
4Playful pixies

Once on each of your turns, you can cause the swarm to assist you in one of the following ways, immediately after you hit a creature with an attack:

  • The attack's target takes 1d6 piercing damage from the swarm.
  • The attack's target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or be moved by the swarm up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice.
  • You are moved by the swarm 5 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice.
It's Your Swarm.

A Swarmkeeper's swarm and spells are reflections of the character's bond with nature spirits. Take the opportunity to describe the swarm and the ranger's magic in play. For example, when your ranger casts gaseous form, they might appear to melt into the swarm, instead of a cloud of mist, or the arcane eye spell could create an extension of your swarm that spies for you. Such descriptions don't change the effects of spells, but they are an exciting opportunity to explore your character's narrative through their class abilities. For more guidance on customizing spells, see the "Personalizing Spells" section in chapter 3.

Also, remember that the swarm's appearance is yours to customize, and don't feel confined to a single appearance. Perhaps the spirits' look changes with the ranger's mood or with the seasons. You decide!

features.name: Swarmkeeper
features.entriesHtml: Feeling a deep connection to the environment around them, some rangers reach out through their magical connection to the world and bond with a swarm of nature spirits. The swarm becomes a potent force in battle, as well as helpful company for the ranger. Some Swarmkeepers are outcasts or hermits, keeping to themselves and their attendant swarms rather than dealing with the discomfort of others. Other Swarmkeepers enjoy building vibrant communities that work for the mutual benefit of all those they consider part of their swarm.

11th-level Swarmkeeper feature

Your Gathered Swarm grows mightier in the following ways:

  • The damage of Gathered Swarm increases to 1d8.
  • If a creature fails its saving throw against being moved by Gathered Swarm, you can also cause the swarm to knock the creature prone.
  • When you are moved by Gathered Swarm, it gives you Cover||3||half cover until the start of your next turn.

15th-level Swarmkeeper feature

You can discorporate into your swarm, avoiding danger. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that damage. You vanish into your swarm and then teleport to an unoccupied space that you can see within 30 feet of you, where you reappear with the swarm.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

features.name: Tools of the Trade
features.entriesHtml: You've learned to interrogate and use implements of torture. You gain proficiency with Torture Tools and the Insight skill. You also have Expertise|XPHB with them.

features.name: Torturer Conclave
features.entriesHtml:
Enshrouded within the radiance of Luyarnha, a conclave of Rangers lies concealed, their solemn duty vowed to the preservation of peace within the walls, regardless of the means. Ever vigilant against the insidious advance of the Scourge, they have honed their inquisitorial craft, recognizing the importance of early prevention of this plague. They achieve this by finding and interrogating victims—and even potential victims—before signs of sickness manifest themselves.

Although these Rangers have been known to serve the clergy and royalty, since the fall of the House of Commons, they are no longer beholden to the fickle desires of any specific lord or lady. Many are now driven by a loftier purpose, one that necessitates the utmost discipline and commitment, for they recognize that if the Scourge is allowed to propagate, it shall wreak havoc upon all they cherish. Yet, some pursue baser ambitions, offering their expertise to those who desire to bend these Rangers to their malevolent will, extracting confessions or inflicting retribution upon adversaries. After all, torture, a practice as ancient as the very bedrock of the earth, is a dreadful instrument, potent enough to shatter even the most indomitable of spirits.

In the throes of battle, these Rangers bring their torturous expertise with them, employing it with merciless precision to break their enemies and methodically subject them to unspeakable agony. They show no mercy to their foes, for they are well aware that none would be extended to them in kind.

Disclaimer.

Please be advised that while some may use torture as a plot device or as a means of gathering information, it is a sensitive and disturbing topic. While the use of torture can be integral to the story being told, which is why it is included in this book, it is important to ensure that everyone at the table comes to an agreement regarding its use prior to the session beginning, and if it's included, whether descriptions should fade to black or be more detailed.

features.name: Torturer Techniques
features.entriesHtml:
You learn to use techniques. Unlike others who require patience and careful preparation, you make use of techniques that are fueled by your magic, letting you employ of Torture Tools in the midst of hunts—no creature too alien or too resolute to escape your methods.

You can use each technique twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can expend one use of your Favored Enemy|Ranger|XPHB|1|XPHB feature (no action required) to regain one use of a technique.

Techniques.

When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or an Unarmed Strike|XPHB while you have Torture Tools in one hand (or a free hand and the presence of Torture Tools at your disposal, such as strapped around your leg), as part of that attack, you can use a technique to enhance it in some way. You can only use a technique once per turn, though you can use different techniques in the same turn, and you can only use one technique per attack.

Empowered Techniques.

When you use a technique, you can empower it by expending a spell slot (no action required). When you do so, you inflict extra damage to the target, and the target subtracts a number of d4s from the saving throws it makes against the technique. The amount of damage and the number of dice subtracted are determined by the level of the spell slot expended, as shown on the following table. You can expend a spell slot up to a level determined by your Ranger level, also shown on the following table. You can also empower a technique if you expend one use of your Favored Enemy feature, which counts as a level 1 spell slot.

Ranger LevelSpell SlotExtra DamageSaving Throw Penalty
3rd1stWisdom mod1d4
5th2nd2 × Wisdom mod2d4
9th3rd3 × Wisdom mod3d4
13th4th4 × Wisdom mod4d4
17th5th5 × Wisdom mod5d4
Techniques.

You learn each of the following techniques. At higher levels, these techniques are improved.

Technique Save DC.

If a technique requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus.

Combing.

You scrape, tear, and flay the victim's body. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d10 Slashing damage.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if you damage a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it begins to decompose, taking Necrotic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. This damage can't be reduced or prevented. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Any extra damage from empowering this technique also applies to this Necrotic damage. A creature can't suffer multiple instances of this effect at once.

Enucleation.

You aim a vicious strike at the target's eye, reducing their vision to a macabre blur. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d6 of the weapon's damage type, and it must make a Constitution saving throw. Creatures with more than two eyes have Advantage|XPHB on this saving throw. On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage|XPHB on Wisdom (Perception) checks and has the Blinded condition against anything further than 60 feet from it for 1 minute. The target repeats this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it has the Blinded condition for the same duration.

Hamstringing.

You slash at the creature's tendons. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d6 Slashing damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its Speed|XPHB reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, its Speed|XPHB becomes 0 for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Nerve Scraping.

You damage the creature's nerves. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d4 Psychic damage and must make a Constitution saving throw.

On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, the target must use its action before moving to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within reach other than itself. If no creature is in reach, it acts normally but randomly determines targets.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails this save two rounds in a row, it subtracts 1d4 from its attack rolls and saving throws for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Throat Chop.

You deliver a fierce cleave to the target's throat, severely impairing its ability to breathe and speak. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage and can't speak or use the Verbal components of spells until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if you hit a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn.

Tympanic Rupture.

You slam the target's ears in an attempt to destabilize it. On a hit, the target takes an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the Deafened condition for 1 minute. A Deafened creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it is disoriented for the duration. While disoriented, the target can't take Reaction|XPHB|Reactions.
rawEntries: You learn to use techniques. Unlike others who require patience and careful preparation, you make use of techniques that are fueled by your magic, letting you employ of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in the midst of hunts—no creature too alien or too resolute to escape your methods.

You can use each technique twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can expend one use of your {@classFeature Favored Enemy|Ranger|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature (no action required) to regain one use of a technique.

rawEntries.name: Techniques
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while you have {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in one hand (or a free hand and the presence of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} at your disposal, such as strapped around your leg), as part of that attack, you can use a technique to enhance it in some way. You can only use a technique once per turn, though you can use different techniques in the same turn, and you can only use one technique per attack.

rawEntries.name: Empowered Techniques
entries: When you use a technique, you can empower it by expending a spell slot (no action required). When you do so, you inflict extra damage to the target, and the target subtracts a number of {@dice d4}s from the saving throws it makes against the technique. The amount of damage and the number of dice subtracted are determined by the level of the spell slot expended, as shown on the following table. You can expend a spell slot up to a level determined by your Ranger level, also shown on the following table. You can also empower a technique if you expend one use of your Favored Enemy feature, which counts as a level 1 spell slot.

rawEntries.name: Techniques
entries: You learn each of the following techniques. At higher levels, these techniques are improved.

entries.name: Technique Save DC
entries: If a technique requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Combing
entries: You scrape, tear, and flay the victim's body. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Slashing damage.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if you damage a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it begins to decompose, taking Necrotic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. This damage can't be reduced or prevented. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Any extra damage from empowering this technique also applies to this Necrotic damage. A creature can't suffer multiple instances of this effect at once.

entries.name: Enucleation
entries: You aim a vicious strike at the target's eye, reducing their vision to a macabre blur. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} of the weapon's damage type, and it must make a Constitution saving throw. Creatures with more than two eyes have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition against anything further than 60 feet from it for 1 minute. The target repeats this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for the same duration.

entries.name: Hamstringing
entries: You slash at the creature's tendons. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Nerve Scraping
entries: You damage the creature's nerves. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage and must make a Constitution saving throw.

On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, the target must use its action before moving to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within reach other than itself. If no creature is in reach, it acts normally but randomly determines targets.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails this save two rounds in a row, it subtracts {@dice 1d4} from its attack rolls and saving throws for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if you hit a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

A {@condition Deafened|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it is disoriented for the duration. While disoriented, the target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

features.name: Depraved Mind
features.entriesHtml:
You've seen the worst depravities that plague this world and have committed most of them. You are immune to the Frightened condition and gain Resistance|XPHB to Psychic damage.

In addition, if a creature attempts to read your mind or telepathically talk to you against your will, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC. On a failed save, it witnesses the horrors within your mind. It takes Psychic damage equal to your level and fails to communicate with you. On a successful save, it can interact with you in this way for 1 minute without making the saving throw.

features.name: Veil of Pain
features.entriesHtml:
When you damage a creature with your torturer techniques, you can attempt to rattle its mind with the pain (no action required). The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC or start dissociating your presence, its mind refusing to acknowledge the anguish you are causing it, only perceiving you as a flicker. You have the Invisible condition to the target for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Mental Agony
features.entriesHtml: You know how to cause pain to your quarry both physically and mentally. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that failed a saving throw against one of your torturer techniques since the start of your last turn makes an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to flourish your blades, smile, or perform a similar terrifying display. The target subtracts 1d10 from its saving throw. Creatures that are immune to the Frightened condition are immune to this effect.

features.name: Coordinated Tactics
features.entriesHtml:
You have an innate understanding of coordinating teamwork. It is represented by your Teamwork Die, which is used in the powers you have from this subclass. The Teamwork Die table shows the die size when you reach certain Ranger levels.

At the start of your turn, roll your Teamwork Die and use that result for it until the start of your next turn when you reroll it.

Coordinated Strikes.

When another creature you can see hits a target with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to roll your Teamwork Die and add the number rolled to the attack's damage against the target. The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.

Coordinated Tactics.

You grant your allies the ability to harmonize their positions on the battlefield. At the start of your turn, after you roll your Teamwork Die you can choose any number of willing creatures within 60 feet of you that can see you. Each of the chosen creatures can take a Reaction|XPHB to move up to a number of feet equal to 5 times the number rolled or up to its Speed|XPHB, whichever is lower. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attack and ignores Difficult Terrain|XPHB.

Until the start of your next turn, each of the chosen creatures gains a bonus to the same check equal to a roll of your Teamwork Die.

features.name: Trail Warden
features.entriesHtml:
Trail wardens are Rangers who have taken an oath. When they lead others into the wilderness, they swear to bring them back safe and sound, but they aren't mere bodyguards or tour guides. Trail Wardens only lead those they deem capable of providing the skills and abilities needed to endure the horrid monsters and grinding conditions of an expedition. Far from civilization's protective grasp, there is no room for dead weight. A single mistake can cost the lives of an entire party.

Trail Wardens are known for their harsh attitude toward others. Some Trail Wardens believe that they must bring the realities of the wilderness into civilization to prevent the careless from joining their expeditions and endangering the group. But once in the wilds, they become nurturing, protective, and insightful as they guide their charges safely through dangerous territory.

entries: Wanting to become a hero is a noble aim, but no one remembers the guy who died of dysentery on his way to the dungeon.

features.name: Tactical Assault
features.entriesHtml:
Your ability to direct the movement and attacks of your allies improves.

Each ally you choose with your Coordinate Tactics feature that can see or hear you gains one of the following benefits of their choice.

Guardian Maneuver.

Until the start of your next turn, the first time the ally takes damage, they can reduce the damage taken by the number rolled on your Teamwork Die.

Recon Maneuver.

When an ally takes a Reaction|XPHB to move, it can take the Hide action as part of that Reaction|XPHB. It gains a bonus to the Dexterity (Stealth) check equal to the number rolled on your Teamwork Die.

features.name: Coordinated Effort

features.name: Group Assault
features.entriesHtml: You coordinate your allies in their attacks against a powerful foe. If you take the Attack action and each attack you make is against the same target, you can choose other creatures within 60 feet of yourself. Each of the chosen creatures gains a bonus to one attack roll and damage roll equal to the number rolled on your Teamwork Die against the same target.

features.name: Swarming Strikes
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can command all of your swarms to make an Attack action instead of just one. Alternatively, a single swarm can attack twice instead of once when it takes the Attack action.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Vermin Lord
features.entriesHtml:
Grow Powerful from Strength in Numbers

Vermin Lords cultivate loyal hordes of disease-bearing rodents to help them battle greater evils. For many of these Rangers, that greater evil is some kind of societal ill, but a rare few see their fellow Humanoids as an infestation that threatens the natural world. Regardless of their goal, they make their homes in sewers, slums, and other forgotten places where they are free to plot against their enemies and tend to their verminkin.

features.name: Verminkin
features.entriesHtml:
You can comprehend and verbally communicate with Tiny Beasts.

As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot to summon vermin swarms. You summon a number of swarms equal to the slot's level for 1 hour. Each swarm is summoned to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of yourself. A swarm uses the Swarm of Vermin stat block.

In combat, each swarm acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction|XPHB on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can command each swarm with a single Bonus Action|XPHB.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Winter Trapper
features.entriesHtml:
Employ Icy Snares to Render Your Quarry Frozen and Helpless

Winter Trappers are masters of control and keep both their adversaries and quarries helpless and at bay. Originating from the Everglacier, these trained hunters are experts at staying upright when others would surely fall, and have learned how to use magic and acrobatics to keep both themselves and their allies out of harm's reach.

features.name: Arctic Predator
features.entriesHtml:
Your archetype's wintry history grants you the following benefits.

Helpless Prey.

When you make an attack against a target that has the Prone condition while you're more than 5 feet away from it, you don't have Disadvantage|XPHB on the attack roll as a result of that condition.

Ice Walker.

Difficult Terrain|XPHB composed of ice or snow doesn't cost you extra movement, and you have Advantage|XPHB on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while in icy or snowy terrain.

features.name: Magic Snare
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can imperceptibly create a magical trap in the ground at your feet. The first Large or smaller creature other than you that enters that space in the next minute springs the trap and must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC; the trap can't be sprung by you or creatures you designate when you create it. On a failed save, a creature takes 2d8 Piercing damage, and its Speed|XPHB is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

A creature that can see Invisible objects (such as one benefiting from See Invisibility or Truesight) can see these traps. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

entries: You have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage.

rawEntries.name: Polar Strikes
entries: When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage to the target, which can take this extra damage only once per turn. When you reach Ranger level 11, this extra damage increases to {@dice 1d6}.

features.name: Hunter's Rime
features.entriesHtml:
Ice rimes you and your prey, protecting you and slowing them. When you cast Hunter's Mark, you gain Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to 1d10 plus your Ranger level.

Additionally, while a creature is marked by your Hunter's Mark, it can't take the Disengage action.

Additionally, while a creature is marked by your {@spell Hunter's Mark|XPHB}, it can't take the {@action Disengage|XPHB} action.

features.name: Winter Walker
features.entriesHtml:
Withstand the Horrors of Frigid Wastelands

Winter Walkers hone their craft in the bleak and frozen wilds of places like Icewind Dale. These ruthless, rimed Rangers hunt monsters that haunt arctic wastelands, eventually becoming frigid terrors themselves. Winter Walkers are well versed in the phenomena of Icewind Dale, including the latent magic of fallen Netherese cities, endemic monsters like yeti and crag cat, and the rising threat of Underdark invaders. Due to their cold pragmatism, terrifying magic, and mastery of the region, Winter Walkers are regarded with equal parts respect and fear. Ten-Towns citizens say that Winter Walkers' frequent exposure to malignant entities gives them their fearsome powers. Many Reghed nomads, on the other hand, believe that nature spirits bestow on Winter Walkers a unique curse.

features.name: Fortifying Soul
features.entriesHtml:
Your experience surviving harrowing environments allows you to bolster your allies in addition to yourself. As a Magic action, choose a number of creatures you can see equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Each chosen creature regains Hit Points|XPHB equal to 1d10 plus your Ranger level and has Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition for 1 hour.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Chilling Retribution
features.entriesHtml:
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force the creature to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target has the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn. While the target is Stunned, its Speed|XPHB is reduced to 0 feet.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Frozen Haunt
features.entriesHtml:
When you cast Hunter's Mark, you can adopt a ghostly, snowy form. This form lasts until the spell ends, and while you are in this form, you gain the following benefits. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB unless you expend a level 4+ spell slot (no action required).

Frozen Soul.

You have Immunity|XPHB to Cold damage. When you first adopt this form and at the start of each of your subsequent turns, each creature of your choice in a 15-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation originating from you takes 2d4 Cold damage.

Partially Incorporeal.

You have Immunity|XPHB to the Grappled, Prone, and Restrained conditions. You can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain|XPHB, but you take 1d10 Force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object. If the form ends while you are inside a creature or an object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space.

You gain Expertise|XPHB in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. Sleight of Hand and Stealth are recommended if you have proficiency in them.

At Rogue level 6, you gain Expertise|XPHB in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

features.name: Sneak Attack
features.entriesHtml:
You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have Advantage|XPHB on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need Advantage|XPHB on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the Incapacitated condition, and you don't have Disadvantage|XPHB on the attack roll.

The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

features.name: Thieves' Cant
features.entriesHtml: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in chapter 2|XPHB|2|Choose Languages.

features.entriesHtml:
Your training with weapons allows you to use the weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties of two kinds of weapons|items|type=simple weapon;martial weapon of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Dagger and Shortbow.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the weapon mastery properties|XPHB|mastery properties of Scimitar and Shortsword.

features.entriesHtml: You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Rogue level or lower.

features.name: Cunning Strike
features.entriesHtml:
You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove 1d6 from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.

If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus.

To use this effect, you must have a Poisoner's Kit on your person.

You can't use this feature if you have the Incapacitated condition.

features.name: Arachnoid Stalker
features.entriesHtml:
Sling Webs and Crawl Walls

A life-changing event, such as being cursed by a drider or being bitten by a dangerously transmuted arachnid, has imbued you with the abilities of a spider. This transformation might have left you physically unchanged, or you may have developed a half-dozen eyes, lanky and hairy limbs, or a set of inhuman mandibles. Whatever the side effects, you can now produce deadly poison and ropes of silken web from your palms, and even scale walls with your fingertips.

features.name: Webbing
features.entriesHtml:
You can magically produce sticky, silken spider webs from your hands as a Bonus Action|XPHB. This web dissolves after 1 minute. When you create the webs, you can use them to do one of the following.

Pull Yourself.

You project a line of web at a point you can see within 30 feet, pulling yourself to that point in a straight line without provoking Opportunity Attack. You can use this benefit as a Reaction|XPHB when you fall to pull yourself up to 10 feet in any direction.

Manipulate Objects.

You can use a line of web to manipulate an object that isn't being worn or carried within 30 feet. For example, you can pull an object to your hand, close a door, or snatch a Small or smaller object weighing less than 10 pounds.

Create Rope.

You create a 60-foot-long Rope of web and anchor it to a point you choose.

Web Spell.

You cast Web without a spell slot as a part of the Bonus Action|XPHB used for this feature (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus). When you cast it using this feature, the webs fill a 5-foot Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube, and the spell's duration becomes 1 minute. You can cast this spell using this feature twice. You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
features.entriesHtml: When you cast Mage Hand, you can cast it as a Bonus Action|XPHB, and you can make the spectral hand Invisible. You can control the hand as a Bonus Action|XPHB, and through it, you can make Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks.

You can control the hand as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, and through it, you can make Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.entriesHtml:
You have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7|XPHB|7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as an Arcane Trickster.

Cantrips.

You know three cantrips: Mage Hand and two other cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard (see that class's section for its list). Mind Sliver and Minor Illusion are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of your cantrips, except Mage Hand, with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

Spell Slots.

The Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

Prepared Spells of 1st+ Level.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells. Charm Person, Disguise Self, and Fog Cloud are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Rogue, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

Changing Your Prepared Spells.

Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability.

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus.

You can use an Arcane Focus as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB for your Wizard spells.

features.name: Magical Ambush
features.entriesHtml: If you have the Invisible condition when you cast a spell on a creature, it has Disadvantage|XPHB on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.
rawEntries: If you have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition when you cast a spell on a creature, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.

features.name: Versatile Trickster
features.entriesHtml: You gain the ability to distract targets with your Mage Hand. When you use the Trip option of your Cunning Strike on a creature, you can also use that option on another creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand.
rawEntries: You gain the ability to distract targets with your {@spell Mage Hand|XPHB}. When you use the Trip option of your Cunning Strike on a creature, you can also use that option on another creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand.

features.name: Spell Thief
features.entriesHtml:
You gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster.

Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC equals your spell save DC. On a failed save, you negate the spell's effect against you, and you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is at least level 1 and of a level you can cast (it doesn't need to be a Wizard spell). For the next 8 hours, you have the spell prepared. The creature can't cast it until the 8 hours have passed.

Once you steal a spell with this feature, you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Assassin
features.entriesHtml:
Practice the Grim Art of Death

An Assassin's training focuses on using stealth, poison, and disguise to eliminate foes with deadly efficiency. While some Rogues who follow this path are hired killers, spies, or bounty hunters, the capabilities of this subclass are equally useful for adventurers facing a variety of monstrous enemies.
rawEntries: {@i Practice the Grim Art of Death}

While some Rogues who follow this path are hired killers, spies, or bounty hunters, the capabilities of this subclass are equally useful for adventurers facing a variety of monstrous enemies.

features.name: Assassin's Tools
features.entriesHtml: You gain a Disguise Kit and a Poisoner's Kit, and you have proficiency with them.

features.name: Assassinate
features.entriesHtml:
You're adept at ambushing a target, granting you the following benefits.

Initiative.

You have Advantage|XPHB on Initiative|XPHB rolls.

Surprising Strikes.

During the first round of each combat, you have Advantage|XPHB on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. If your Sneak Attack hits any target during that round, the target takes extra damage of the weapon's type equal to your Rogue level.

features.name: Infiltration Expertise
features.entriesHtml:
You are expert at the following techniques that aid your infiltrations.

Masterful Mimicry.

You can unerringly mimic another person's speech, handwriting, or both if you have spent at least 1 hour studying them.

Roving Aim.

Your Speed|XPHB isn't reduced to 0 by using Steady Aim.

features.name: Envenom Weapons
features.entriesHtml: When you use the Poison option of your Cunning Strike, the target also takes 2d6 Poison damage whenever it fails the saving throw. This damage ignores Resistance|XPHB to Poison damage.
rawEntries: When you use the Poison option of your Cunning Strike, the target also takes {@damage 2d6} Poison damage whenever it fails the saving throw. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage.

features.name: Death Strike
features.entriesHtml: When you hit with your Sneak Attack on the first round of a combat, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw (8 plus your Dexterity modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus), or the attack's damage is doubled against the target.

features.name: Blade of Radiance
features.entriesHtml:
The Blades of Radiance, also called Steel Saints, are known to be one of the most lethal orders of the Church. In order to become a blade, one must be a devout follower of the faith, as only those who would die for the cause are deemed worthy. Prospective members are trained within the walls of the Church, taking on the clergy as their new kin and discarding whatever familial bonds they might have held onto. Their zealous fervor grants them unrivaled powers on the battlefield, wielding massive weapons as if they were mere toys, infusing their blade with divine powers, and breaking down their foes one by one.

The Blades of Radiance receive an incredibly diverse range of missions. The most brutal of their members handle gruesome matters in a lethal fashion, whereas those of a more empathetic temperament are tasked with protecting their fellows. Despite this sundry in character, they all share one goal: safeguarding the Church and its members, no matter what.

features.name: Divine Blessings
features.entriesHtml:
Your devotion to eradicating enemies of the Church manifests as righteous power. You have a pool of Divine Points equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 point). You regain all expended points when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB. In addition, whenever you kill an Aberration, Beast, Fiend, or Undead of CR 1/2 or higher with your sanctified blade, you regain 1 expended Divine Point.

Radiance Save DC.

If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus.

You can expend Divine Points to use the following features.

  • Armor of the Faithful.
  • Divine Inspiration.
  • Rend the Blasphemous.

rawEntries: You can expend Divine Points to use the following features.

items.name: Armor of the Faithful
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature targets you with an attack, you can expend 1 Divine Point to force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker must choose a new target or the attack has no effect. In addition, the attacker can't target you with an attack until the start of your next turn. This feature doesn't protect you from areas of effect, such as the explosion of a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell.

items.name: Divine Inspiration
items.entry: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) or a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, you can expend 1 Divine Point to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new result. You can choose to use this feature after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

items.name: Rend the Blasphemous
items.entry: On your turn after you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with your sanctified blade, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 Divine Point to let the divine hand guide you. Make a weapon attack with it against a creature within your reach. You gain a bonus to your attack roll equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

features.name: Sanctified Champion
features.entriesHtml:
Your intense training bears fruit. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

Whenever you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, you can perform a ritual on a melee weapon you are proficient with that deals Piercing or Slashing damage, sanctifying it. It becomes your sanctified blade, and you can only have one such blade at a time. The blade has the Finesse|XPHB property for you, and attacks made with it against Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead ignore Resistance|XPHB to damage.
rawEntries: Your intense training bears fruit. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can perform a ritual on a melee weapon you are proficient with that deals Piercing or Slashing damage, sanctifying it. It becomes your sanctified blade, and you can only have one such blade at a time. The blade has the {@itemProperty Finesse|XPHB} property for you, and attacks made with it against Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to damage.

features.name: Righteous Armament
features.entriesHtml:
Your faith gives you the power to rebel against fate itself. You learn the following features that use your Divine Points.

  • Chains of Judgement.
  • Divine Retaliation.
  • Erupting Blades.
rawEntries: Your faith gives you the power to rebel against fate itself. You learn the following features that use your Divine Points.

items.name: Chains of Judgement
items.entry: When you hit a creature with your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to create holy chains around the creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take Radiant damage equal to your Wisdom modifier and have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Divine Retaliation
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature damages you with a melee attack while you are wielding your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to make a melee attack with your blade against the creature. You gain a bonus to the damage roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.

items.name: Erupting Blades
items.entry: When you hit a creature with an attack that could apply your Sneak Attack damage, you can forgo damaging the creature with your Sneak Attack and expend 2 Divine Points to cause radiant blades to fall on the battlefield. The target and each creature in a 45-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} originating from the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Radiant damage equal to your Sneak Attack damage. On a successful save, a target takes half damage.

features.name: Saintly Revelations
features.entriesHtml:
You experience revelations, showing you how to channel divine energy to embolden your blade. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Cleric spell|spells|level=0|class=cleric|components & miscellaneous=|subschool=osteomancy list.

In addition, you always have the Heroism, Protection From Evil and Good, and Shield of Faith spells prepared. With this feature, you can cast these spells at will, targeting only yourself, without a spell slot or components. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Starting at Rogue level 17, when you cast these spells using this feature, they don't require Concentration|XPHB. However, you can only have one spell cast from this feature active at a time; if you cast a second one, the first spell ends.

features.name: Final Judgement
features.entriesHtml:
Your sanctified blade becomes imbued with holy power, granting you the following benefits.

  • Divine Spirits.
  • Radiant Blade.
rawEntries: Your sanctified blade becomes imbued with holy power, granting you the following benefits.

items.name: Divine Spirits
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while wielding the blade, you can cast {@spell Spirit Guardians|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. Creatures within the area of the spell, for the purpose of your Sneak Attack, are considered within 5 feet of an ally of yours. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend 3 Divine Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

items.name: Radiant Blade
items.entry: You can speak a command word (no action required) to cause your blade to emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet. The light lasts until you speak the command word again or you stow your weapon. While emitting light in this way, the weapon is considered a magic weapon, and attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 2d4} Radiant damage on a hit.

features.name: Hair Trigger
features.entriesHtml:
You gain proficiency with Blackpowder Pistol. In addition, when you roll Initiative|XPHB and don't have Disadvantage|XPHB on that roll, you can immediately take a Reaction|XPHB for one of the following options:

  • Make one attack with a weapon or Unarmed Strike|XPHB.
  • Move up to your Speed|XPHB without provoking Opportunity Attack.
  • A controlled mount moves up to its Speed|XPHB without provoking Opportunity Attack.
  • Take the Dodge or Utilize action.

In addition, when you roll {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} and don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that roll, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} for one of the following options:

Take the {@action Dodge|XPHB} or {@action Utilize|XPHB} action.

features.name: Highway Rider
features.entriesHtml:
A Steed Makes the Best Partner in Crime

Stalking the backroads, the Highway Rider strikes fear into the heart of every traveler and penny-pinching merchant. They run down their prize astride a swift and loyal steed—and then make a quick getaway.

features.name: Ride Them Down
features.entriesHtml: You don't need Advantage|XPHB on the attack roll to Sneak Attack if you or a controlled mount you ride moves at least 20 feet, and you don't have Disadvantage|XPHB on the attack roll.
rawEntries: You don't need {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the attack roll to Sneak Attack if you or a controlled mount you ride moves at least 20 feet, and you don't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the attack roll.

features.name: Trusty Mount
features.entriesHtml:
You always have the Find Steed spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components, and your spellcasting ability for it is Intelligence.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

features.name: Horse Lord
features.entriesHtml:
You can spend 1 minute grooming and caring for your mount, at the end of which it gains a number of Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice your Rogue level.

In addition, your cunning extends to your steed. While you control a mount, it can take one of the following actions as a Bonus Action|XPHB: Dash, Disengage, or Dodge.

features.name: True Grit
features.entriesHtml: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.
rawEntries: You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

features.name: Desperado
features.entriesHtml: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB and not killed outright, you can use your Hair Trigger feature immediately before you fall Unconscious.
rawEntries: When you are reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and not killed outright, you can use your Hair Trigger feature immediately before you fall {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.

features.name: Charming Presence
features.entriesHtml: You can take the Influence action as a Bonus Action|XPHB. Additionally, choose one of the following skills: Deception, Intimidation, or Performance, or Persuasion. You have proficiency in that skill.
rawEntries: You can take the {@action Influence|XPHB} action as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. Additionally, choose one of the following skills: {@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, or {@skill Performance|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}. You have proficiency in that skill.

features.name: House Agent
features.entriesHtml:
The drow houses of Menzoberranzan conspire against each other in a great game of status and sabotage that expands far beyond the city's limits. When a house needs a specialized tool to further its interests without arousing suspicion, it calls in a house agent.

Using the tools and training of their sponsor, a house agent is a master infiltrator, capable of insinuating themself into their target's life and striking while their target's back is turned.
