features.name: Physical Specimen
features.entriesHtml:
Your patron has enhanced your physical form to improve your utility as a host and pawn. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, once per Long Rest|XPHB, choose a number of the following benefits up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one) that lasts until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. Whenever you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, you can choose one of your selected benefits and replace it with another from this list.

  • Your Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum increases by an amount equal to your Warlock level.
  • You gain Darkvision with a range of 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet.
  • You Speed|XPHB increases by 5 feet.
  • You have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Poisoned condition.
  • Your jump distance is tripled, and you gain a Climb Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB.
  • Add your Charisma modifier to your Strength (Athletics) check or Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

features.name: Spell Siphon
features.entriesHtml:
Your patron has taught you to siphon magic from your enemies and make it your own. Immediately after a creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force the creature to make a Charisma saving throw. The DC equals your spell save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't cast a spell again until 8 hours have passed. While this effect lasts, if the spell was at least level 1 and of a level you can cast, you have that spell prepared.

The maximum number of spell levels you can have siphoned at once equals 1 plus your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). If you have the Incapacitated condition or die, you lose all siphoned spells. When you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you lose all siphoned spells.

features.name: The Parasite Patron
features.entriesHtml:
Become One with a Cosmic Being

Your patron is a cosmic parasite, draining the vitality of entire peoples and worlds. Upon forging a pact with such a patron, you become host to one of its nascent offspring. As you grow in power, the boundary between your identity and the parasitic larva within blurs.

features.name: Symbiotic Sentinel
features.entriesHtml: Your patron remains alert to threats to its host at all times. You can't be surprised|XPHB and you have Advantage|XPHB on Initiative|XPHB rolls. You also have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

features.name: Spawn Pawn
features.entriesHtml:
You always have the Dominate Person spell prepared. You can also cast it once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

In addition, taking damage can't break your Concentration|XPHB on Dominate Person. When a creature succeeds on its saving throw, it takes Psychic damage equal to your Warlock level.

features.name: Larval Regeneration
features.entriesHtml:
When you die, a larval parasite bursts from your corpse. You control the parasite. The parasite uses the Rat stat block except it has your Hit Points|XPHB; Hit Point Dice|XPHB; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. It can't cast spells. In addition, it has the following ability:

Burrowing Possession.

As a Magic action, the parasite can cause a Humanoid within 5 feet of it to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice) against your Warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, the parasite burrows into the creature, dealing Piercing damage equal to your Warlock level. While burrowed inside a creature, the parasite can't take any action, Bonus Action|XPHB, or Reaction|XPHB, has Cover|XPHB|Total Cover, and has Immunity|XPHB to all damage except Psychic damage.

On each of the creature's subsequent turns, it can use its action to make a Constitution saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC. If the creature succeeds, the parasite is ejected from its body and into an unoccupied space of the creature's choice within 5 feet of it. If the parasite is burrowed inside the creature when the creature's turn ends, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to twice your Warlock level. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it immediately dies, the parasite disappears, and you take over the body of the Humanoid as if you had been targeted by the Reincarnate spell and rolled the species the Humanoid had been.

If you are returned to life, such as by the Revivify spell, your parasite immediately disappears.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Context Switch
features.entriesHtml:
Your patron grants you the ability to play a harmful trick on others while saving yourself from harm. When a creature makes a melee attack against you, you can use your Reaction|XPHB and choose a creature within 5 feet of you. If the creature is unwilling, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure (or if it is willing), it magically swaps places with you and becomes the target of the attack. If the attack hits the target, the target takes the damage instead of you, and if the target was an enemy, it has Disadvantage|XPHB on attack rolls until the start of your next turn.

You can use this Reaction|XPHB a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Nimble Trickery
features.entriesHtml:
You gain proficiency in Sleight of Hand if you don't already have it. When you make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check to swap an item with another item that has similar dimensions, you have Advantage|XPHB on the check.

When you reach 6th level, you can swap an object with an unattended object of similar dimensions up to 30 feet away by succeeding on a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check. When you reach 14th level, you can replace the target object with an illusion rather than exchanging it for a real object. The illusory duplicate lasts for 1 minute. Once you use this aspect of Nimble Trickery, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB or expend a Pact Magic spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of it.

features.name: Trickster
features.entriesHtml:
Imbue Life with a Touch of Chaos

From the halls of the fey to the antics of Loki, there are entities who embody the primal nature of chaos. Your pact draws upon one of these powers, perhaps a creature with an aspect of whimsy or a deity relishing in tricks and ploys. Your patron asks you to sow chaos and delight in mischief. If you squint, you can almost make sense of the method behind their seeming madness.

features.entriesHtml: When you use your Context Switch class feature, you can choose a creature within 30 feet of you (rather than within 5 feet of you). If you do not choose to do this, you can instead choose for the creature you swap with to have Disadvantage|XPHB on its save. If your target (regardless of its distance from you) fails its save, you can choose to have the Invisible condition until the end of your next turn or until immediately after you make an attack roll, deal damage, or cast a spell (whichever comes first).

features.name: Painful Unreality
features.entriesHtml:
Your patron teaches you how to see beyond the veil of unreality. You automatically succeed on your Intelligence (Investigation) check when you take the Study action to determine if something is illusory.

In addition, when a creature interacts with an Illusion spell you cast and fails to determine that it is illusory, you can choose to force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature interacting with the Illusion spell takes 4d10 Psychic damage and has the Stunned condition until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

It has Disadvantage|XPHB on all d20 checks until the end of its next turn, and you and your allies have Advantage|XPHB on all attack rolls and d20 checks you make against it.

You can use this effect once, and you regain it when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB.

Having once been mortal, these ancient patrons know firsthand the paths of ambition and the routes past the doors of death. They eagerly share this profane knowledge and other secrets with those who work their will among the living.

features.name: Grave Touched
features.entriesHtml:
Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic, granting you the following benefits.

Arcane Necrosis.

Necrotic damage from your attacks, Warlock spells, and Warlock features ignores Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage. Once per turn when you cast a spell that deals damage, you can change that spell's damage type to Necrotic.

Dreaded Necrosis.

When you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal Necrotic damage while using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the Necrotic damage the target takes. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

Undead Endurance.

You don't gain Exhaustion levels from dehydration, malnutrition, or suffocation. In addition, you don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

features.name: Necrotic Husk
features.entriesHtml:
Your connection to undeath saturates your body. You gain the following benefits.

Necrotic Resilience.

You have Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage. While using your Form of Dread, you have Immunity|XPHB to Necrotic damage.

Unholy Resuscitation.

If you drop to 0 Hit Points and don't die outright, you can cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking Necrotic damage equal to 2d10 plus your Charisma modifier on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Your Hit Points then change to twice your Warlock level, and you gain 1 Exhaustion level.

Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Vestige Companion
features.entriesHtml:
The vestige manifests, drawing strength from your pact. It uses the Vestige Companion stat block and is a Celestial, Fiend, or Undead (choose when you gain this feature). You determine what the vestige looks like, but regardless of its form, the vestige bears features indicating its supernatural origin. For example, you might decide your vestige is an oversize floating skull etched with sigils, a circle of glowing runes, or a constantly shifting abstract shape. The vestige is Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die.

The Vestige in Combat.

In combat, the vestige acts during your turn. It can move and use its Reaction|XPHB on its own, but the only action it takes is the Dodge action unless you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the Attack action to command the vestige to take the Vestige's Strike action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, the vestige acts on its own and isn't limited to the Dodge action.

Disappearance of the Vestige.

When the vestige drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it disappears. You can spend 1 minute performing a magical ceremony to manifest the vestige again; it reappears with its maximum Hit Points|XPHB in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. As a Magic action, you can temporarily dismiss the vestige to a pocket dimension. As a Magic action while it is temporarily dismissed, you can cause the vestige to reappear in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. Whenever the vestige drops to 0 Hit Points|XPHB or disappears into the pocket dimension, it leaves behind in its space anything it was wearing or carrying.

Vestige Companion.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can summon the vestige in a new form, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You choose its appearance and whether it is a Celestial, Fiend, or Undead. If the vestige is already manifested from this feature, its form changes to the new one.

features.name: Vestige Patron
features.entriesHtml:
Wield the Remnants of a Dying God's Power

Your pact draws on the power of a dying god, a being once worshipped by countless followers but now abandoned and forgotten. This dying god, known as a vestige, might have been benevolent, evil, or strange and unknowable, but now it is driven to regain its former power. The vestige needs your help, and it is willing to share its remaining strength with you.

features.name: Vestige Spells
features.entriesHtml:
The magic of your Vestige Companion ensures you always have certain spells ready. Select one of the following Cleric domains: Cleric, Cleric, Cleric, or Cleric. The Domain Spells of your chosen domain are Warlock spells for you. When you reach a Warlock level equal to a Cleric level listed on the Domain Spells table for the domain you have chosen, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

For example, if you chose the Cleric for this feature, when you reach Warlock level 3, you would have the Guiding Bolt, Magic Weapon, Shield of Faith, and Spiritual Weapon spells prepared.

In addition, while within 30 feet of your Vestige Companion, you have Resistance|XPHB to the same damage types as the vestige.

The vestige then teleports to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of it. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Semblance of Life
features.entriesHtml:
Your Vestige Companion continues to grow in strength, and with your assistance, it can briefly adopt a more powerful form. Depending on the vestige's type, you can take a Magic action while the vestige is within 90 feet of you to shape-shift it for 1 hour into one of the following forms: Celestial Spirit (Celestial vestige; see the Summon Celestial spell in the Player's Handbook|XPHB|9), Fiendish Spirit (Fiend vestige; see the Summon Fiend spell in the Player's Handbook|XPHB|9), or Undead Spirit (Undead vestige; see the Summon Undead spell in the Player's Handbook|XPHB|9). The vestige's game statistics are replaced by the spirit's stat block, and the spell's level is equal to half your Warlock level (round down; maximum level 9), but the vestige retains its personality, Divine Power Bonus Action|XPHB, Hit Points|XPHB, and Hit Point Dice|XPHB.

The vestige gains a number of Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to the Hit Points|XPHB of the spirit form. These Temporary Hit Points|XPHB vanish if any remain after 1 hour, and the transformation ends early if it has no Temporary Hit Points|XPHB left.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Arcane Recovery
features.entriesHtml:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you're a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels' worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Spellcasting
features.entriesHtml:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7|XPHB|7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list|spells|class=Wizard later in the class's description.

Cantrips.

You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

Spellbook.

Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting Identify. You determine the book's appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

Spell Slots.

The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+.

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability.

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus.

You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus|XPHB for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook.

The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a Spell Scroll, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

Copying a Spell into the Book.

When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it's of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

Copying the Book.

You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

features.name: Abjurer
features.entriesHtml:
Shield Companions and Banish Foes

Your study of magic is focused on spells that block, banish, or protect—ending harmful effects, banishing evil influences, and protecting the weak. Abjurers are sought when baleful spirits require exorcism, when locations must be guarded against magical spying, and when portals to other planes of existence must be closed. Adventuring parties value Abjurers for the protection they provide against a variety of hostile magic and other attacks.

features.name: Arcane Ward
features.entriesHtml:
You can weave magic around yourself for protection. When you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, you can simultaneously use a strand of the spell's magic to create a magical ward on yourself that lasts until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. The ward has a Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum equal to twice your Wizard level plus your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead, and if you have any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's Hit Points|XPHB. If the damage reduces the ward to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, you take any remaining damage. While the ward has 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it can't absorb damage, but its magic remains.

Whenever you cast an Abjuration spell with a spell slot, the ward regains a number of Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice the level of the spell slot. Alternatively, as a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can expend a spell slot, and the ward regains a number of Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice the level of the spell slot expended.

Once you create the ward, you can't create it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

If this damage reduces the ward to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, the warded creature takes any remaining damage. If that creature has any Resistances or Vulnerabilities, apply them before reducing the ward's Hit Points|XPHB.

features.name: Spell Breaker
features.entriesHtml:
You always have the Counterspell and Dispel Magic spells prepared. In addition, you can cast Dispel Magic as a Bonus Action|XPHB, and you can add your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus to its ability check.

When you cast either spell with a spell slot, that slot isn't expended if the spell fails to stop a spell.

features.name: Spell Resistance
features.entriesHtml: You have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws against spells, and you have Resistance|XPHB to the damage of spells.

features.name: Bibliomancy
features.entriesHtml:
A spellbook is a Wizard's prized possession. Even the least experienced apprentice knows that each spell's formula must be carefully recorded, understood, and memorized to cast a spell properly. For the typical Wizard, the symbols, words, and equations in a spellbook are a means to an end.

For Bibliomancers, the language of magic is the key to the building blocks of the universe. This tradition believes that a spell's formula holds more than the gathering and shaping magical energy, that the underlying properties of reality itself are illustrated through a spell. By unlocking the mechanisms that construct spells, these Wizards can slowly unlock the riddle of the universe.

features.name: Book Learning
features.entriesHtml: You have an arcane connection to all books, be they tablets or tomes, allowing you to unravel their secrets. If you touch an object containing a script for 1 minute, you learn a basic, working knowledge of the script's contents unless that information is hidden by a code or cypher. If the book or script is a magic item or magical object, you learn its properties and how to use it, whether it requires Attunement|XPHB, and how many charges it has, if any. You learn whether any ongoing spells are affecting the item and what they are. If the item was created by a spell, you learn that spell's name.

features.name: Edit Spell
features.entriesHtml:
Choose a spell in your spellbook that is level 1 or higher. When you prepare that spell, you can give it one or more of the following benefits:

  • The spell save DC of the chosen spell, if any, increases by 1.
  • If that spell deals damage, you can change that damage's type to a different one of your choice.
  • If that spell requires a saving throw, you can change that saving throw to Intelligence.

You can prepare the chosen spell multiple times, choosing different benefits for each preparation. Each modified version of the spell counts against your prepared spells.

When you make these changes, you can alter the spell's name. For example, Burning Hands changed to deal Cold damage and require an Intelligence saving throw might be named Mind Freeze.

When you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can change your chosen spell. When you change the chosen spell, the benefits to the previous chosen spell end and you no longer have the altered versions prepared.

If that creature is the only target of the spell, you can cast the spell on it without needing to maintain Concentration|XPHB.

features.name: Master of Words
features.entriesHtml:
When you prepare spells, pick two spells from levels 1 to 5 to weave into a linked, powerful spell you can prepare as a single spell. The level of the linked spell is equal to the combined level of the two spells chosen and can't exceed 6.

The chosen spells must have a Verbal component and must have a casting time of one action.

As a Magic action, you can cast the linked spell, and the effects of both spells occur at the same time.

features.name: Bladesinger
features.entriesHtml:
Wield Weapon and Wizardry in Elegant Tandem

Bladesingers master a tradition of wizardry that incorporates swordplay and dance. In combat, a Bladesinger uses intricate, elegant maneuvers that fend off harm and allow the Bladesinger to channel magic into devastating attacks and a cunning defense. Many who have observed a Bladesinger at work remember the display as one of the more beautiful experiences in their life—a glorious dance accompanied by a singing blade.

Bladesinging is associated with the ancient elven societies that first mastered the art and coined the term. Even today, most Bladesingers still hail from old elven realms, such as Myth Drannor, or from non-elven societies that share land and history with elves, such as the Silver Marches. Wherever they hail from, Bladesingers take their talents all across the Realms to help common people and perform heroic deeds. Most communities greet the arrival of a Bladesinger as a good omen.

features.name: Bladesong
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you invoke an elven magic called the Bladesong, provided you aren't wearing armor or using a Shield.

The Bladesong lasts for 1 minute and ends early if you have the Incapacitated condition, if you don armor or a Shield, or if you use two hands to make an attack with a weapon. You can dismiss the Bladesong at any time (no action required).

While the Bladesong is active, you gain the following benefits. You can invoke the Bladesong a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You regain one expended use when you use Arcane Recovery.

Agility.

You gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1), and your Speed|XPHB increases by 10 feet. In addition, you have Advantage|XPHB on Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks.

Bladework.

Whenever you attack with a weapon with which you have proficiency, you can use your Intelligence modifier for the attack and damage rolls instead of using Strength or Dexterity.

Focus.

When you make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration|XPHB, you can add your Intelligence modifier to the total.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Conjurer
features.entriesHtml:
Step Across Space and Call Creatures from Thin Air

A Conjurer considers distance and matter to be flexible guidelines rather than physical laws. Conjurers master magic that moves creatures instantly through space and summons creatures to fight on their behalf.

features.name: Splintered Summons

features.name: Daemonologist
features.entriesHtml:
Steal Scraps of Divine and Infernal Power

Through theological study, or perhaps an induction into a secretive cabal, Daemonologists have learned to cast divine magic without the need for faith or bargains. Their spellbooks are scribed with prayer fragments and blasphemous hymns, enabling them to siphon scraps of power from both Arch Seraphs and Arch Daemons. From their heretical research, they've come to believe such otherworldly beings are two sides of the same divine kin.

Daemonology is rarely practiced. If the nature of their abilities is discovered, they risk being persecuted not only by superstitious folk but also by celestial and infernal powers.

features.name: Stolen Secrets
features.entriesHtml:
You have uncovered or stolen secret power from agents of the Arch Daemons and Arch Seraphs. You gain one Eldritch Invocation|optionalfeatures|feature type=EI of your choice.

Prerequisites.

If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. If an invocation has a Warlock level prerequisite, you use your Wizard level instead. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Wizard level 5.

Replacing and Gaining Invocations.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.

You gain an additional invocation when you reach Wizard levels 6 and 14.

You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

Intelligent Invocations.

You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for your invocations.

features.name: Borrowed Tongues and Hides
features.entriesHtml:
Your ability to siphon power from Celestials and Fiends is enhanced. You gain the following benefits.

Arch Daemon Boon.

While you are siphoning power from Arch Daemons, you have Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage. In addition, Fiends that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

Arch Seraph Boon.

While you are siphoning power from Arch Seraphs, you have Resistance|XPHB to Radiant damage. In addition, Celestials that know languages can understand your speech and you can understand theirs, even if you do not share a language.

Switch Sides.

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can change which power you are siphoning from. Once you switch, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Unearthly Countenance
features.entriesHtml:
As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you adopt an infernal or celestial countenance for 10 minutes. For the duration, your appearance gains aspects of the power you choose. You gain the following benefits.

Commanding Presence.

You have Advantage|XPHB on Charisma checks.

Improved Spells.

When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell from the Arch Daemon or Arch Seraph table, the spell is cast as if you had spent a spell slot of one level higher.

Unearthly Wings.

You gain a Fly Speed|XPHB of 60 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage only.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Diviner
features.entriesHtml:
Learn the Secrets of the Multiverse

The counsel of a Diviner is sought by those who want a clearer understanding of the past, present, and future. As a Diviner, you strive to part the veils of space, time, and consciousness. You work to master spells of discernment, remote viewing, supernatural knowledge, and foresight.

features.name: Portent
features.entriesHtml:
Glimpses of the future begin to press on your awareness. Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any D20 Test|XPHB made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn.

Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you lose any unused foretelling rolls.

features.name: Expert Divination
features.entriesHtml: Casting Divination spells comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your spellcasting efforts. When you cast a Divination spell using a level 2+ spell slot, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.

features.name: The Third Eye
features.entriesHtml:

Darkvision.

You gain Darkvision with a range of 120 feet.

Greater Comprehension.

You can read any language.

See Invisibility.

You can cast See Invisibility without expending a spell slot.

features.entriesHtml:
Entrance and Beguile Others

An Enchanter's magic clouds or captivates minds. Some Enchanters use their abilities to encourage peace and soften cruelty, while others use their mind-altering magic for selfish ends.

features.entriesHtml:

In addition, when you make an ability check with the chosen skill, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1).

features.name: Hypnotic Presence
features.entriesHtml:
Your charming words and enchanting gaze can enthrall another creature. As a Magic action, choose one creature that you can see within 10 feet of yourself. If the target can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Charmed condition for 1 minute or until the target is more than 10 feet away from you, the target can neither see nor hear you, or the target takes damage. While Charmed, the target has the Incapacitated condition and a Speed|XPHB of 0.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

When you use a spell slot to cast an Enchantment spell|spells|school=E, such as Charm Person, that can be cast with a higher-level spell slot to target an additional creature, you can increase the spell's effective level by 1.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Instinctive Charm
features.entriesHtml:
When a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to force the attacker to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the attack misses instead, and if there is another creature within range of the attack other than the attacker, the attacker targets that creature with the triggering attack, using the same attack roll. If multiple creatures are within the attack's range, you choose which one to target.

Once you take this Reaction|XPHB, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore your use of it by casting an Enchantment spell|spells|school=E with a spell slot.

features.name: Alter Memories
features.entriesHtml:
You can make a creature unaware of your magical influence. When you cast an Enchantment spell|spells|school=E that imposes the Charmed condition using a spell slot, you can choose one creature targeted by the spell. That creature remains unaware of being Charmed by you.

In addition, once before the spell ends, you can take a Magic action to force the chosen creature to make an Intelligence saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can make the creature lose a number of hours of its memories equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 hour lost). You can make the creature forget less time, and the amount of time can't exceed the duration of your Enchantment spell|spells|school=E.

features.name: Evoker
features.entriesHtml:
Create Explosive Elemental Effects

Your studies focus on magic that creates powerful elemental effects such as bitter cold, searing flame, rolling thunder, crackling lightning, and burning acid. Some Evokers find employment in military forces, serving as artillery to blast armies from afar. Others use their power to protect others, while some seek their own gain.

features.name: Potent Cantrip
features.entriesHtml: Your damaging cantrips affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When you cast a cantrip at a creature and you miss with the attack roll or the target succeeds on a saving throw against the cantrip, the target takes half the cantrip's damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the cantrip.

features.name: Sculpt Spells
features.entriesHtml: You can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your evocations. When you cast an Evocation spell that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 plus the spell's level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the spell, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

features.name: Overchannel
features.entriesHtml:
You can increase the power of your spells. When you cast a Wizard spell with a spell slot of levels 1–5 that deals damage, you can deal maximum damage with that spell on the turn you cast it.

The first time you do so, you suffer no adverse effect. If you use this feature again before you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you take 2d12 Necrotic damage for each level of the spell slot immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores Resistance|XPHB and Immunity|XPHB.

Each time you use this feature again before finishing a Long Rest|XPHB, the Necrotic damage per spell level increases by 1d12.

features.name: Illusionist
features.entriesHtml:
Weave Subtle Spells of Deception

You specialize in magic that dazzles the senses and tricks the mind, and the illusions you craft make the impossible seem real.

features.name: Improved Illusions
features.entriesHtml:
You can cast Illusion spells without providing Verbal components, and if an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, the range increases by 60 feet.

You also know the Minor Illusion cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. You can create both a sound and an image with a single casting of Minor Illusion, and you can cast it as a Bonus Action|XPHB.

features.name: Phantasmal Creatures
features.entriesHtml: You always have the Summon Beast and Summon Fey spells prepared. Whenever you cast either spell, you can change its school to Illusion, which causes the summoned creature to appear spectral. You can cast the Illusion version of each spell without expending a spell slot, but casting it without a slot halves the creature's Hit Points|XPHB. Once you cast either spell without a spell slot, you must finish a Long Rest|XPHB before you can cast the spell in that way again.

features.name: Illusory Self
features.entriesHtml:
When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to interpose an illusory duplicate of yourself between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 2+ spell slot (no action required).

features.name: Illusory Reality
features.entriesHtml: You have learned to weave shadow magic into your illusions to give them a semi-reality. When you cast an Illusion spell with a spell slot, you can choose one inanimate, nonmagical object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a Bonus Action|XPHB while the spell is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute, during which it can't deal damage or give any conditions. For example, you can create an illusion of a bridge over a chasm and then make it real and cross it.

features.name: Imaskarcanist
features.entriesHtml: Imaskarcanists have learned the ancient secrets of Deep Imaskar, a once-human society living in the deepest depths of the Underdark. Through these eldritch arts—taught to the Deep Imaskari by sentient artifacts called the Imaskarcana—they have mastered the power of Unlight, a brilliant, destructive, and infectious energy that can be used to both heal and destroy. With this power, the Deep Imaskari have launched a war of conquest to bring light to every corner of the Underdark. Each Imaskarcanist must decide for themself whether to aid the conquering army or use their power against it and preserve the comforting darkness of the world below.

features.name: Learning the Secrets of Unlight
features.entriesHtml:
Unlight is a rare form of magic known to very few. You can roll on or choose a result from the Secrets of Unlight table to inspire how your character learned about this secret magic.

Secrets of Unlight.

features.name: Unlight Adept
features.entriesHtml:
You know how to weave Unlight into your damaging spells. When you cast a spell that deals Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage, you can change that damage type to Radiant.

In addition, Dim Light|XPHB created by spells you cast is Bright Light|XPHB instead.

features.name: Unlight Invigoration
features.entriesHtml: You can imbue creatures with Unlight drawn from your own energy, making them stronger and fiercer. As a Bonus action|XPHB, choose a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you and roll one or two of your Hit Point Dice|XPHB. Those dice are then expended. The target gains Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to the total rolled plus your Intelligence modifier, and until the target has no Temporary Hit Points|XPHB, it has Advantage|XPHB on Strength checks and sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius.

features.name: Unlight Restoration
features.entriesHtml:
You can wield the restorative effects of Unlight to heal injuries and remove harmful effects. As a Bonus action|XPHB, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you and roll one or two of your Hit Point Dice|XPHB. Those dice are then expended. The target regains Hit Points|XPHB equal to the total rolled and sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 10-foot radius until the end of its next turn.

If you expended two Hit Point Dice|XPHB, you can choose to end one of the following conditions on the target: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Poisoned. If you do, the target does not regain Hit Points|XPHB.
rawEntries: You can wield the restorative effects of Unlight to heal injuries and remove harmful effects. As a {@variantrule Bonus action|XPHB}, choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you and roll one or two of your {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}. Those dice are then expended. The target regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the total rolled and sheds {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius until the end of its next turn.

If you expended two {@variantrule Hit Point Dice|XPHB}, you can choose to end one of the following conditions on the target: {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. If you do, the target does not regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

features.name: Secrets of Deep Imaskar
features.entriesHtml:
Your research into the secrets of the Imaskarcana grants you the following benefits.

  • Imaskarcana Lore.

    You can attune yourself to a magic item as a Magic action. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

  • Piercing Unlight.

    Your spells ignore Resistance|XPHB to Radiant damage.

  • Unlight Resilience.

    You gain Resistance|XPHB to Radiant damage.

  • Imaskar Seals.

    You always have the Glyph of Warding spell prepared and can cast it once without a spell slot. When you cast the spell in this way, you don't need Material components, you cast the spell as if using a spell slot equal to the highest Wizard spell slot you have. Any previous glyph you created in this way is broken, and its spell ends without being triggered. You regain the ability to cast Glyph of Warding in this way when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Doom Of Unlight
features.entriesHtml:
You can curse your enemies with corrosive Unlight, and the only escape from the curse is physical violence or an explosive death.

When a creature takes Radiant damage from a spell you cast, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to curse that creature with Unlight. The creature makes a Constitution save against {@dcYourSpellSave}. On a failure, the creature is cursed. Until the curse ends, the target suffers the following effects:

  • The target emits Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius.
  • Attack rolls against the target have Advantage|XPHB.
  • At the start of each of the target's turns, it takes Radiant damage equal to your character level.
  • The target has Advantage|XPHB on Strength checks and melee attack rolls.
  • If the target hits another creature with a melee attack roll, the target can repeat the Constitution save, ending this curse on a success.
  • If the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, it explodes. Roll a number of d8 equal to half your character level. Creatures in a 10-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation centered on the target take Radiant damage equal to the total rolled.

Once you have attempted to curse a creature using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB or until you expend a level 6+ spell slot (no action required).

features.name: Magic Missile Mage
features.entriesHtml:
Cast Magic Missile Better Than Anyone

Magic Missile is a staple wizard spell, beloved for its versatility and unerring accuracy. As a Missile Mage, however, your fondness for the spell borders on obsession. Your studies focus entirely on this spell, exploring every aspect of its casting, resulting in new augmentations and greater power.

features.name: Magic Missile Savant
features.entriesHtml:
Add the Magic Missile spell to your spellbook for free. Your expertise in this spell grants you the following benefits.

Extra Darts.

When you cast Magic Missile, you create an extra dart of magical force. You create two extra darts at Wizard level 6, three extra darts at Wizard level 10, and four extra darts at Wizard level 14.

Free Casting.

You can cast Magic Missile without a spell slot. You can do so a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain one expended use when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

Penetrating Darts.

Your Magic Missile darts bypass any effect, such as the Shield spell, that specifically blocks the Magic Missile spell.

features.name: Versatile Missiles
features.entriesHtml:
You can accurately guide your Magic Missile darts to strike a target wherever you choose. When you cast Magic Missile, you can add one of the following Versatile Missile effects to a target struck by the darts. Each effect has a cost, which is the number of darts you must forgo to add the effect to the target. You can add different effects to different targets, paying the cost for each effect separately.

Trip Missile (Cost: 1 Dart).

The target must succeed on Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Prone condition.

Blinding Missile (Cost: 3 Darts).

The target must succeed on Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Blinded condition until the start of your next turn.

Stunning Missile (Cost: 5 Darts).

The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the Stunned condition until the start of your next turn.

features.name: Shield of Missiles
features.entriesHtml:
When you cast Magic Missile, you can direct the darts in a tight orbit around yourself, creating a protective 10-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation originating from you, which lasts for up to 1 minute.

You gain a bonus to your Armor Class|XPHB equal to the number of darts orbiting you (maximum bonus of +5). Whenever a creature within 120 feet misses you with an attack roll, one dart strikes the attacker, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you by one.

Whenever the Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation enters the space of a creature you can see and whenever a creature you can see enters the Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation or ends its turn there, you can strike the target with any number of darts orbiting you, dealing damage as normal and decreasing the number of darts orbiting you. You can damage a creature with the Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation only once per turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 3+ spell slot (no action required).

features.name: Arcane Artisan
features.entriesHtml:
You have dedicated your studies to creation and the magic surrounding it. You gain the following benefits.

Bonus Cantrip.

You know the Mending cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

Creation Savant.

You gain proficiency with three Artisan's Tools of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can replace your proficiency with one type of Artisan's Tools with a different type of Artisan's Tools of your choice.

Mage Craft.

Your exceptional wit and aptitude allow you to do more with less time. While crafting using a set of Artisan's Tools with which you have proficiency, you can subtract your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) from the number of hours you must work each day, allowing you to complete a full day's work in 7 hours or less (to a minimum of 2 hours).

features.name: Materializer
features.entriesHtml:
Easily Create and Destroy Matter as a Master Artisan and Arcanist

Some Wizards abandon the limitations set by magic schools and instead focus on the binding force that holds everything together. These mages spend their efforts weaving and recreating matter from thin air to create art as well as utility. They value the craftsmanship taught by artisans around the world and consider their skills and creations to be a form of magic all its own.

Some arcanists focus on altering the living, whereas Materializers focus on creating and enhancing the inanimate. These mages see beauty in the possibility presented by raw materials and are found as readily studying ancient lore as they are in the center of a bustling forge. Many followers of this tradition take great care and pride in their Component Pouches and find great kinship among Bards, artists, and other craftsmen.

features.name: Minor Creation
features.entriesHtml:
When you cast a level 1+ spell, you can magically create a Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube of inanimate material of your choice that is no larger than 5 feet on a side. The Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube appears in an unoccupied space you can see on the ground within 30 feet of you, or it appears magically connected to another Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube within that range that you created with this feature. Once you reach Wizard level 10, the range increases to 60 feet. A Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube created in this way weighs a number of pounds equal to 5 times its length on a side, regardless of its material. The Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes can support up to 10 times their weight, potentially serving as a bridge, and they can provide cover for creatures behind them.

You can have a total number of these Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes in existence at a time equal to your Wizard level. You can dismiss any number of the Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes of your choice as a Bonus Action|XPHB. Otherwise, a Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube disappears after 1 hour or if it takes any damage. The Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes are objects that have an AC equal to 10 + your Intelligence modifier, 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point, and Immunity|XPHB to Force damage.

Cube Detonation.

When you take a Bonus Action|XPHB to dismiss one or more of the Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes, you can choose to detonate any of them instead, destroying them. Each creature within 10 feet of a detonated Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cube must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature takes Force damage equal to 1d6 + half your Wizard level (round down) on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. You can detonate a total number of Cube [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cubes—all at once or with multiple separate Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions—equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1), and you regain all expended uses of doing so when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. You can also restore uses of it by expending a level 1+ spell slot (no action required), regaining a number of uses equal to the slot's level.

features.name: Material Enhancement
features.entriesHtml:
Your attention to both magic and mundane detail gives you a heightened understanding and control over them. As a Magic action, you can touch a weapon, suit of armor, or other object. Until the end of your next Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB, the object becomes magical if it isn't already, and gains your choice of up to two of the following benefits:

  • (Weapon Only) The wielder of the weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it; this bonus increases to +2 when you reach Wizard level 10 and +3 when you reach Wizard level 14. If the weapon already granted a bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, the wielder must choose whether to use that bonus or the one granted by this feature when attacking with it.
  • (Armor Only) The wearer of the armor gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class|XPHB; this bonus increases to +2 when you reach Wizard level 10 and +3 when you reach Wizard level 14. If the armor already granted a bonus to AC, the wearer must choose whether to use that bonus or the one granted by this feature when calculating its Armor Class|XPHB.
  • (Armor Only) The armor doesn't impose Disadvantage|XPHB on Dexterity (Stealth) checks if it normally would.
  • The object sheds Bright Light|XPHB in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light|XPHB for an additional 20 feet. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, a creature holding the object can cause it to stop or resume shedding this light.
  • The object's weight is halved. If the object is a suit of armor, it doesn't have a Strength requirement if it normally would. If it's a weapon with the H|XPHB|Heavy property, it doesn't impose Disadvantage|XPHB on the wielder's attack rolls as a result of that property.
  • When a creature throws the object, it flies back to the creature's hand immediately after hitting or missing its target.
  • You change any of the object's colors, smells, and textures.

You can use this feature twice, expending one use for each benefit you give an object. You regain all expended uses of this feature when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB. Once you give an object a benefit in this way, you can't give that benefit to an object again until you regain your expended uses of this feature.

features.name: Dematerialize
features.entriesHtml: Your spells deal double damage to objects and structures, and whenever you deal damage to a Construct, it takes an extra 1d8 Force damage.

features.name: Rematerialize
features.entriesHtml:
When you see a Large or smaller nonmagical object or structure be destroyed within 60 feet of you, you can take a Reaction|XPHB to cause its debris to magically vanish. Once within the next 8 hours, you can take a Magic action to recreate the item, causing it to reappear intact in an unoccupied space you choose within 60 feet of you.

If the item is recreated in the air, it immediately falls. Any creature below it must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet the item fell before reaching it. The amount of damage dealt is based on the item's size: Small or smaller (1d6), Medium (2d6), or Large (3d6). On a successful save, a creature takes half as much Bludgeoning damage. Unless the object is at least one size smaller than a creature it falls on, that creature is pushed to the nearest unoccupied space.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Necromancer
features.entriesHtml: You explore the cosmic forces of life, death, and undeath. As a Necromancer, you learn to manipulate the energy that animates all creatures. As you progress, you learn to use magic to drain the life force from a creature, transforming its vital energy into magical power. Many see Necromancers as menacing or villainous, though not all Necromancers are evil. Nevertheless, the manipulation of life and death is considered taboo in many societies.

Necrotic Resistance.

Grim Harvest.

entries: When you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot, choose yourself or a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself to gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the level of the spell slot plus your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1 {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB|Temporary Hit Point}).

features.name: Grave Power
features.entriesHtml:
You have discovered more necromantic insights and inscribed them into your spellbook. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

Grave Resilience.

When you use Arcane Recovery|Wizard|XPHB|1|XPHB, your Exhaustion level, if any, decreases by 1.

Overwhelming Necrosis.

Damage from your Wizard spells and Wizard features ignores Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic damage.

features.name: Undead Thralls
features.entriesHtml:
You always have Summon Undead prepared and can cast it once without expending a spell slot.

When you cast Summon Undead without a spell slot, you can regain Hit Points|XPHB equal to half the summoned creature's total Hit Points|XPHB, but doing so halves the creature's Hit Points|XPHB. Once you cast the spell without a spell slot, you must finish a Long Rest|XPHB before you can cast the spell in this way again.

features.name: Undead Secrets
features.entriesHtml:
You have learned more secrets about the nuances of life and death. When you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, you can expend a level 4+ spell slot to protect yourself from death. Until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB, the next time you would drop to 0 Hit Points|XPHB, your Hit Points|XPHB instead change to a number equal to ten times the spell slot expended.

In addition, immediately after you take damage and are Bloodied|XPHB after taking that damage but not killed outright, you can take a Reaction|XPHB and teleport to an unoccupied space up to 60 feet from yourself, and each creature within 10 feet of the space you left takes 2d10 Necrotic damage.

features.name: Bolster Undead
features.entriesHtml: As a Bonus Action|XPHB, choose any number of Undead you have created or summoned with a Necromancy spell that are within 60 feet of yourself. Those Undead each gain Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to your Wizard level. Once an Undead gains Temporary Hit Points|XPHB from this feature, it can't gain them in this way again for the next 24 hours.

Once an Undead gains {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} from this feature, it can't gain them in this way again for the next 24 hours.

features.name: Death's Master
features.entriesHtml:
Abstruse rituals within your spellbook allow you mastery over forces of death. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

Harvest Power.

When you use Grim Harvest, the creature that gains Temporary Hit Points|XPHB gains one of the following benefits of your choice, which lasts until the end of the target's next turn:

  • The target has Advantage|XPHB on attack rolls.
  • The target has Advantage|XPHB on the next saving throw it makes.

features.name: Forbidden Knowledge
features.entriesHtml:
In your study of proscribed power, you learn Deep Speech|XPHB or another language of your choice.

In addition, choose a level 1 spell from the Warlock spell list. You always have it prepared. You can change your chosen spell when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Intrusion
features.entriesHtml:
Your search into the forbidden reaches beyond the universe yields great power but comes at the risk of letting something from beyond intrude into your reality.

You have an Intrusion Die, which starts at a d6, that can change as you use your features. The die can increase or decrease, along this progression of die sizes: d2, d3, d4, d6, d8, d10, d12.

The size maximum for your Intrusion Die is its starting size, which increases by one step when you reach Wizard levels 5 (d8), 11 (d10), and 17 (d12).

When you use a feature that risks Intrusion, roll your Intrusion Die. On a 2 or higher, no Intrusion occurs, and the Intrusion die reduces in size one step on the progression.

On a roll of 1, the Intrusion Die rises in size one step, and you roll on the Intrusion table to determine what happens as reality fractures. Intrusions use your spell save DC.

The Intrusion Die increases in size by one step (up to its starting size) when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB, and it resets to its starting size when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. Additionally, you can focus alien potency into your spells. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can risk Intrusion to choose one of the following.

Overwhelming Mind.

One target of the spell has Disadvantage|XPHB on the first saving throw made against it.

Seeking Eye.

You have Advantage|XPHB on the first attack roll you make for the spell.

1d12Effect
1You feel a presence behind you that whispers incomprehensible things into your soul. Until the end of your next turn, you can only do one of the following on a turn: take an action, a Bonus Action|XPHB, or move.
2Space twists and melts in a 30-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation around you. Each creature (including you) in the area struggles against the warping of reality. An affected creature's Speed|XPHB is halved until the end of your next turn.
3The nearest other creature within 60 feet of you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take Necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Intrusion Die (at its starting size), and you regain a number of Hit Points|XPHB equal to the damage dealt.
4Reality tears in your space until the end of your next turn. You and each creature that can see the tear must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition while the tear exists.
5One of your arms warps into an alien appendage, such as a distorted version of an arm or a twisting tentacle, for 1 minute. You can make Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes with the limb using your spell attack bonus. Instead of the normal damage, roll a number of your Intrusion dice (at its starting size) equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus. The target takes Acid damage equal to the total rolled.
6Alien landscapes overlay your vision, giving you the Blinded condition until the end of your next turn.
7Unnatural thoughts disorient you, giving you the Incapacitated condition until the end of your next turn.
8You experience an instant of terrible clarity. You take Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Intrusion Die (at its starting size), and for 1 minute, your spell save DC is increased by 2.
9You regain an expended spell slot of level 5 or lower (your choice), and you take Necrotic damage equal to twice the slot's level. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way.
10When you cause this Intrusion and at the end of each of your turns for 1 minute, pulses in the fabric of space fill a 15-foot Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation originating from you, giving you and each creature in it the Prone condition.
11For 1 hour, you hear whispered, disembodied thoughts of hateful scorn directed at you. While you can hear the whispers, you have Disadvantage|XPHB on ability checks and saving throws that rely on Wisdom.
12An Aberration or a Fiend with a CR equal to your Wizard level or lower (GM's choice) appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. The GM decides the creature's attitude (Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile/Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent/Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly) and actions.

features.name: Occultist
features.entriesHtml:
Seek Beyond the Stars for Forbidden Knowledge

Wizardry urges the relentless pursuit of knowledge that pushes every boundary in search of greater power and understanding, but some boundaries are never meant to be crossed. Occultists care not for these limitations, peering behind cosmic veils, devouring forbidden secrets, and pushing their understanding of spellcraft until reality itself tears open. It is from the strange, alien realms that are revealed which they draw even greater power, shattering all limits no matter the eldritch consequences.

features.name: Reality Tear
features.entriesHtml: Choose a spell of level 3 or lower from the Warlock spell list. You always have the spell prepared. You can change your chosen spell when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. When you cast the spell, you can risk Intrusion to remove the need to Concentration|XPHB|Concentrate on it, and the spell ends after 1 minute or its normal duration, whichever is shorter. Additionally, you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to cast the spell once without a spell slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Occult Presence
features.entriesHtml:
When you cause an Intrusion, you can roll twice on the Intrusion table and choose which result to use, and you can negate the Intrusion by gaining 1 Exhaustion level. Additionally, you gain one of the benefits below, and you can change your chosen benefit when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to change your chosen benefit.

Alien Consciousness.

You gain Immunity|XPHB to the Charmed and Frightened conditions, and you can't be possessed.

Cosmic Resistance.

You gain Resistance|XPHB to Necrotic and Psychic damage.

Spatial Domination.

You gain a Fly Speed|XPHB equal to your Speed|XPHB and can hover.

features.name: Beyond Space
features.entriesHtml:
The nature of distance and location is revealed for the lie that it is. You always have the Scrying spell prepared.

When you cast Scrying, you can risk Intrusion to choose one of the following.

All Knowing.

Treat your connection to a target creature as if you have part of its body.

All Seeing.

Cast the spell as an action instead of its normal casting time.

When you cast Scrying, during the spell's duration, as a Magic action you can cause an automatic Intrusion (and increase the die's size one step, up to its starting size) to teleport yourself, and any willing creatures within 10 feet of you, to unoccupied spaces you can see through the scrying sensor.

features.name: Anatomical Expert
features.entriesHtml: Your pursuit of osteomancy has required many hours studying the anatomy of a myriad of creatures. You gain proficiency in the Medicine skill, and when you make a Wisdom (Medicine or Survival) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). In addition, when these checks concern a creature that possesses a skeleton, you have Expertise|XPHB in that skill, even if you don't have proficiency in the Survival skill.

In addition, when these checks concern a creature that possesses a skeleton, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that skill, even if you don't have proficiency in the {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill.

features.name: Brittle Bone Armor
features.entriesHtml:
You learn the basics of osteomancy, using it for protection. As an action, if you're not wearing armor or wielding a Shield, you can force a frame of bones out of your body to protect you, granting you Temporary Hit Points|XPHB equal to twice your Wizard level that last for 1 hour.

While you have these Temporary Hit Points|XPHB, you gain Resistance|XPHB to Piercing and Slashing damage, and you have a +2 bonus to AC.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest|XPHB unless you expend a spell slot of level 2 or higher (no action required) to restore your use of it.

features.name: Osteomancer
features.entriesHtml:
Osteomancers are powerful Wizards who understand the power that can be harvested from bones. Often said to be cursed and talked about under cover of night, this sort of magic makes the uneducated shiver and the scholar morbidly curious. Those who have the cunning, bravery, or simple foolishness to pursue research in this field find themselves rewarded with afflicted knowledge. These accursed souls are known as Osteomancers.

The abilities of an Osteomancer are unsettling, if not terrifying to most. Due to their focus on manipulating bones, a topic that is cloaked in mystery and taboo, regular folks regard them as cursed and malevolent beings. Those who see their magic at work have compared it to witnessing a puppet master—bending and twisting enemies to their whim. Many people fail to realize that an Osteomancer's favorite puppet is themselves and that they will readily desecrate their own body in order to crush their opponent.

features.name: Bone Puppetry
features.entriesHtml:
As a Magic action, you target one creature you can see within 60 feet of you that has a skeleton. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or you take total and precise control of its skeleton. Until the end of the creature's next turn, it takes only the actions you choose and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do. In the creature's efforts to resist your command, attack rolls it makes against its allies have Disadvantage|XPHB, and its allies have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws from effects caused by the creature.

You can only have one such creature under your control at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB.

features.name: Skeletal Mastery
features.entriesHtml:
You are a master of your own body. You have the following benefits.

  • Many Forms.
  • Skeletal Control.
rawEntries: You are a master of your own body. You have the following benefits.

items.name: Many Forms
items.entry: You can reshape your bones, including those of your face, to appear as a completely different person. You can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. When you cast this spell using this feature, it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}, and you can only use the Change Appearance or Natural Weapons options.

items.name: Skeletal Control
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can dissolve or restore your own skeleton. While boneless, you can move yourself through sheer muscular and magical control. In this form, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 10 feet, and you can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. Further, you are considered as having the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, can't use your hands, and can't attack or cast spells. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can regenerate the bones in your hands to exert finer control over them until the end of your next turn.

features.name: Improved Bone Puppetry
features.entriesHtml:
You've enhanced your mastery over skeletal manipulation. When a creature fails its saving throw against your Bone Puppetry feature, your control of the target lasts for 1 minute. The target can't resist your command; it doesn't have Disadvantage|XPHB on attacks against its allies, nor do its allies have Advantage|XPHB on saving throws against effects caused by the target. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. You must concentrate on this feature as you would concentrate on a spell, and damage can't break your Concentration|XPHB.

Once under your control, when the target repeats the saving throw against your Bone Puppetry, you can choose to expend one additional use of the feature to give the creature Disadvantage|XPHB on the save. You must decide to do so before seeing the result of the roll.

features.name: Alchemical Knowledge
features.entriesHtml: You gain a set of Alchemist's Supplies. You have proficiency with it and can use it as an Arcane Focus. Additionally, you can use Alchemist's Supplies instead of the normal tool to craft a magic item.

features.name: Philosopher
features.entriesHtml:
Distill the Essence of Creation

Philosophers have focused their study of wizardry on the fundamental nature of existence and reality. They seek the most quintessential truths of creation and manipulate those forces and substances through alchemical practice. Through understanding, deconstruction, and reconstruction, they master the natural energies of the world around them and alter it to their will.

Every Wizard who walks the steps of the Philosopher does so to solve some specific problem, even if only at first. The Philosophical Pursuits table offers challenges or goals that set you onto your study of alchemical magic.

1d12Guiding Goal
1Someone close to you is lost in time, the planes, or some other esoteric state of being. Unraveling the nature of reality is your path to finding them.
2You suffered a debilitating ailment or injury and turned to the study of magic to deconstruct the impairment's nature and transmute it.
3Your teacher was killed by a rival Philosopher, and you must learn all you can of that discipline to protect yourself and bring them to justice.
4The rediscovered research of a missing mage unlocked the first secrets of your understanding but contains many more you can't yet decipher.
5Wizardry provides a path to immense power, but you know an even greater state of being awaits your ascension.
6You encountered a material with miraculous properties, and you can't rest until you discover the secret of its creation.
7Your sibling's soul was separated from their body in a spell gone wrong, and you cannot forgive yourself until you make them whole.
8You were a stage performer who wowed audiences with magical acts, and you seek the ultimate magic trick to become a legend.
9You come from an impoverished hometown and wish to utilize the transmutation of metals to bring prosperity to your community.
10In your pursuit to be closer to the gods, you have sought the secrets of creating new life forms in your own image.
11You were raised to revere the four elements, and you hypothesized that mastering the stuff of existence will bring harmony to them all.
12You had aspirations of joining the military and rising through the ranks, believing that the magic of reality can be used as a weapon of war.
rawEntries: {@i Distill the Essence of Creation}

Philosophers have focused their study of wizardry on the fundamental nature of existence and reality. They seek the most quintessential truths of creation and manipulate those forces and substances through alchemical practice. Through understanding, deconstruction, and reconstruction, they master the natural energies of the world around them and alter it to their will.

Every Wizard who walks the steps of the Philosopher does so to solve some specific problem, even if only at first. The Philosophical Pursuits table offers challenges or goals that set you onto your study of alchemical magic.

rawEntries.caption: Philosophical Pursuits
rows: Someone close to you is lost in time, the planes, or some other esoteric state of being. Unraveling the nature of reality is your path to finding them.
You suffered a debilitating ailment or injury and turned to the study of magic to deconstruct the impairment's nature and transmute it.
Your teacher was killed by a rival Philosopher, and you must learn all you can of that discipline to protect yourself and bring them to justice.
The rediscovered research of a missing mage unlocked the first secrets of your understanding but contains many more you can't yet decipher.
Wizardry provides a path to immense power, but you know an even greater state of being awaits your ascension.
You encountered a material with miraculous properties, and you can't rest until you discover the secret of its creation.
Your sibling's soul was separated from their body in a spell gone wrong, and you cannot forgive yourself until you make them whole.
You were a stage performer who wowed audiences with magical acts, and you seek the ultimate magic trick to become a legend.
You come from an impoverished hometown and wish to utilize the transmutation of metals to bring prosperity to your community.
In your pursuit to be closer to the gods, you have sought the secrets of creating new life forms in your own image.
You were raised to revere the four elements, and you hypothesized that mastering the stuff of existence will bring harmony to them all.
You had aspirations of joining the military and rising through the ranks, believing that the magic of reality can be used as a weapon of war.

features.name: Quintessence
features.entriesHtml:
You have learned the fundamental process of dissolution. You know the Dissolution cantrip. A creature or object you reduce to 0 Hit Points|XPHB with the cantrip is destroyed. If the target was Small or larger, it dissolves into a measure (1 ounce) of crystalline powder called Quintessence. You can have a maximum amount of Quintessence equal to twice your Intelligence modifier at one time (mimium of 2 measures). If you create more, the oldest measure vanishes. You can use Quintessence you are touching in the following ways.

Material Component.

When you cast a spell, you can expend Quintessence to serve as the spell's Material components up to a value of 100 GP per Quintessence expended.

Reagent.

When you scribe a spell into your spellbook, or when you use Alchemist's Supplies to craft a magic item, you can expend Quintessence to serve as 50 GP worth of material for the task per Quintessence expended.

Vitriolic Enhancement.

When you cast a spell that deals damage, you can expend 1 Quintessence as an additional Material component to change one damage type the spell deals to Force.

features.entriesHtml: You can purify your Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 to amplify your spells. When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can expend 1 Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 as a Material component to increase the level of the spell slot by 1, up to level 9. The maximum Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 you can expend in this way on a given spell is half of your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus (rounded up).

You always have the Creation and Fabricate spells prepared, and you can cast each spell once without expending a spell slot, regaining the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest|XPHB. When you cast a spell using this feature, you can cast the spell as an action rather than its normal casting time. You can also cast the spells normally using spell slots of the appropriate level. Additionally, when you cast Creation, you can expend a number of Quintessence|Wizard|XPHB|Philosopher|CrookedMoon24|3|CrookedMoon24 up to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1) to multiply the spell's duration by 1 plus the amount expended.
